written: 2026-10-31, after OWN_TRAJECTORY_DEV_RESULT_20261031.md (own_trajectory robust on 48/67 expert db:cells; most NWICU failures were care-unit interval undercoverage of the DtACI interval; HCO3 < 18 marginal O/E 0.67-0.69 under static marginals) and before any online-marginal result.
disclosure: same development databases, MIMIC samples, cohort, split and own_trajectory model as the preceding rules; the online distribution settings are the frozen v12 part C ones (threshold_event_candidates_20261029.json), not tuned here.
question: Do online marginal distributions (frozen online point correction + Mondrian MultiQT) calibrate the per-cell marginals better than static ones, and does the dependence layer still beat independent cells over them?

online_marginal.deployment_clock: per hospital, osler_jepa.deployment_clock with seed stable_seed(cell, 0, hospital, 'clock'), as jepa_deployment_form_dev.deploy (identical scored rows; warm-up stays unscored); an outcome is used only after label_available_hr
online_marginal.point_correction: online_point_correction with site_adaptive_point_amendment_20261024.json (via jepa_gate_rule_20261022.json), scale = median |error| on MIMIC selection patients
online_marginal.distribution: mondrian_multiqt_stream per hospital: day-one scores = signed errors of MIMIC conformal patients divided by the v2 quintile scale fitted on MIMIC selection patients; uniform calibration weights (event rows carry no day-one covariates, as the JEPA deployment form); categories = tail8 bins of the current value from MIMIC calibration patients; MultiQT settings of threshold_event_candidates_20261029.json
online_marginal.members: 50 values per row: the row's issued quantiles interpolated at levels (k - 0.5) / 50, k = 1..50 (all inside the 0.01-0.99 grid)

static_marginal: the own_trajectory static point + empirical quantiles of its signed errors on MIMIC conformal patients at the same 50 levels

joint.copula: Gaussian copula as own_trajectory_joint_dev_rule_20261031.json (pairwise Spearman of own_trajectory static errors on MIMIC selection patients)
joint.coupling: ensemble copula coupling (Schefzik et al. 2013): each cell's 50 sorted marginal values are assigned to members by the ranks of the latent draws; independent = the same with identity-correlation draws; joint and independent therefore share identical marginals

blocks.cross_target: per anchor and horizon: the targets labelled and scored there (>= 2)
blocks.across_horizons: per anchor and target: the horizons labelled and scored there (>= 2)

primary_readouts.marginal_interval: per database:cell, the online distribution's central 90% interval [q0.05, q0.95] passes the interval gate (external_value_conditional_interval_audit.interval_report, GATE_AXES interval axes, bounds [0.87, 0.93]); robust if >= 80% of 5 samples; compared with the own_trajectory DtACI interval of own_trajectory_dev_s*_20261031.json on the same scored rows
primary_readouts.joint_vs_independent: per test database and block, over the online marginals: variogram score (order 0.5, standardized by the calibration-error IQR), patient-cluster bootstrap 95% CI of joint - independent; joint better if the upper bound < 0; robust if better in >= 80% of samples

secondary_readouts: variogram and energy score of online-joint vs static-joint (does online calibration help the multivariate forecast)
single-event marginal O/E, static vs online, on the same rows, for map < 65, heart_rate > 120, potassium >= 6.0, bicarbonate < 18, creatinine rise >= 0.3, glucose > 180
joint event O/E and Brier for the four pairs of joint_forecast_dev_rule_20261031.json, online-joint vs online-independent vs static-joint (pairs with >= 30 joint events)
